key_points: Problem as defined (PD-1): shipment notices sent from ORG-A to ORG-B via handoff H-1 are being rejected; in a 3-record reject-log sample, 2 are tagged LOC_UNKNOWN (notices N-1, N-2) and 1 is tagged EVENT_ORDER (notice N-3) (F-01, F-02, F-03, E-01).

PD-1's root_problem text asserts as settled fact that the notices' location/reference codes do not match ORG-B's current reference data, but verification found this is only an unverified assumption (A-LOC-UNKNOWN-MECHANISM): hypothesis H-REFERENCE-DATA-MISMATCH is SUPPORTED, not CONFIRMED, is contradicted by E-02, and the underlying mechanism question (U-REJECT-MECHANISM-SPECIFICITY) is OPEN/DEFERRED to VOB-U-REJECT-MECHANISM-SPECIFICITY.

The original request (CL-01, stakeholder SH-REQ) was to let an AI agent auto-fix and resubmit rejected notices; the same stakeholder later gave a different, non-authoritative account (CL-02/E-02) blaming carrier-system flakiness and proposing blind resubmission with no data fix - these two stakeholder claims conflict and neither is confirmed.

DEFINE gate result was CONDITIONAL_PASS (recent_event seq 48), deferring the mechanism unknown as VOB-U-REJECT-MECHANISM-SPECIFICITY; subsequent verification (seq 83) passed layer 1 but failed the semantic check 'root_problem_evidence_consistency'.

What was actually released (SD-1 release_scope): the diagnose_reject_cause:DA-REJ work item (reject-cause distribution from the reject-log) and the monitor_reject_rate:H-1 work item (reject-rate monitoring), both marked DONE in the plan.

The compare_reference_data:DA-REJ action - the direct test of whether the mismatch mechanism is real - was NOT released; it is withheld pending resolution of VOB-U-REJECT-MECHANISM-SPECIFICITY, which lies outside this release's scope.

Final decision: RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, with no items on hold; the release proceeds on the diagnosis and monitoring outputs while explicitly flagging the unresolved root-cause question and other open items as known limitations rather than blocking release.
limitations_explained: The root-cause mechanism is unconfirmed: whether LOC_UNKNOWN rejects are caused by a reference-data mismatch (H-REFERENCE-DATA-MISMATCH, SUPPORTED) or by upstream data-quality problems at ORG-A (H-UPSTREAM-DATA-QUALITY, SUPPORTED) remains an open question; the direct test (compare_reference_data:DA-REJ) was withheld because VOB-U-REJECT-MECHANISM-SPECIFICITY is still OPEN.

The evidence base is a single 3-record sample from DA-REJ, and DA-REJ's broader completeness is UNKNOWN; sample-size adequacy (U-SAMPLE-SIZE-ADEQUACY) is unresolved, so the 2:1 LOC_UNKNOWN-to-EVENT_ORDER split (M-LOC-UNKNOWN-SHARE = 0.667) may not represent the full reject population.

The single EVENT_ORDER reject (N-3) is unexplained: it is unknown whether it shares the same root cause as the LOC_UNKNOWN rejects or is a distinct sequencing defect (U-EVENT-ORDER-CAUSE, VOB-R-2), and this question is unaffected by what was released.

A structural fix - a scheduled reference-data sync or shared lookup feed between ORG-A and ORG-B to prevent recurring LOC_UNKNOWN rejects - was identified as the way to remove the root cause but is explicitly marked not feasible within the available contest time, so interim rejects are expected to continue.

PD-1's root_problem narrative itself did not pass semantic verification (failed check: semantic:root_problem_evidence_consistency) because it states a disputed mechanism as fact; the release proceeds anyway under RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION rather than being held for this.

Two unresolved verification obligations exist: VOB-U-REJECT-MECHANISM-SPECIFICITY (HIGH impact, blocks compare_reference_data:DA-REJ, required BEFORE_RELEASE but deferred) and VOB-R-2 (MEDIUM impact, about the EVENT_ORDER reject, also required BEFORE_RELEASE but still OPEN and intersecting release scope non-critically).

The problem (PD-1) is that shipment notices sent from ORG-A to ORG-B over handoff H-1 are being rejected; a 3-record sample from the carrier reject log (DA-REJ, evidence E-01) showed 2 rejects tagged LOC_UNKNOWN and 1 tagged EVENT_ORDER. The requester (SH-REQ) first asked for an AI agent to auto-fix and resubmit rejects (CL-01), then gave a conflicting, non-authoritative account blaming a flaky carrier system and proposing blind resubmission (CL-02/E-02). The DEFINE gate issued a CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring the core mechanism question (reference-data mismatch vs. upstream data-quality defect) as VOB-U-REJECT-MECHANISM-SPECIFICITY, and later verification flagged that PD-1's text states the mismatch as settled fact when it is really only an unconfirmed assumption/hypothesis. Given this, the release delivers only the diagnosis and monitoring work (reject-cause distribution and reject-rate tracking over H-1), while withholding the direct mechanism test (compare_reference_data:DA-REJ). The final decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, with nothing held back from release but several explicit known limitations attached: the small/uncertain-completeness sample, the unresolved root-cause mechanism, the unexplained EVENT_ORDER reject, and the infeasibility of a structural reference-data-sync fix within the available time.</summary>
